title: Factorization and cocycle identities of horseshoe defects
statement:
Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], S and T short exact sequences in C,
and F a morphism from S to T. Let IA, IB, IC and JA, JB, JC be injective resolutions
[def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the three terms of S and T respectively. Let
alpha, beta and alpha', beta' be chain maps between the corresponding resolutions,
with zero composites, with short exact rows in every nonnegative degree, and with
all four augmentation squares commuting. Let phiA and phiC be prescribed chain maps
between the first and third resolutions respectively, lifting the first and third
components of F. Let t be a family of maps from IB in degree n to JB in degree n,
commuting with both outer row squares in every degree. Then there exist maps E from IC in degree n to JA in degree n+1, and e from S.X3
to JA in degree zero, satisfying these four identities (all composition below is diagrammatic):
(1) beta E alpha' is t followed by the target differential minus the source differential
followed by t in the next degree; (2) S.g e alpha' in degree zero is the difference
between the augmentation followed by t and the prescribed middle augmentation;
(3) the IC augmentation followed by E in degree zero equals e followed by the JA differential;
(4) the IC differential followed by E in the next degree is minus E followed by
the JA differential in the next degree.

proof.text: The differential defect D annihilates alpha and is annihilated by beta', by the two outer squares and the chain-map identities. Descend along the source epic beta and lift through the target monic alpha', using exactness; this gives E.
Expand the differential of D using square-zero differentials. Precompose by beta and postcompose by alpha'; cancel the epic and monic maps. This gives the signed cocycle identity for E.
The augmentation defect w annihilates S.f and is annihilated by beta' in degree zero, using the augmentation squares and the two squares of F. Descend along S.g and lift through alpha' to obtain e.

Compute the augmentation followed by D in degree zero both using the E factorization and using w. The differentials kill the augmentation maps. Cancel S.g and alpha' in degree one to prove the augmentation identity for E and e.

theorem horseshoe_defect_factorization
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (S T : ShortComplex C) (hS : S.ShortExact) (_hT : T.ShortExact) (F : S ⟶ T)
    (IA : InjectiveResolution S.X₁) (IB : InjectiveResolution S.X₂)
    (IC : InjectiveResolution S.X₃) (JA : InjectiveResolution T.X₁)
    (JB : InjectiveResolution T.X₂) (JC : InjectiveResolution T.X₃)
    (α : IA.cocomplex ⟶ IB.cocomplex) (β : IB.cocomplex ⟶ IC.cocomplex)
    (α' : JA.cocomplex ⟶ JB.cocomplex) (β' : JB.cocomplex ⟶ JC.cocomplex)
    (hαβ : α ≫ β = 0) (hαβ' : α' ≫ β' = 0)
    (hα : IA.ι ≫ α = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map S.f ≫ IB.ι)
    (hβ : IB.ι ≫ β = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map S.g ≫ IC.ι)
    (hα' : JA.ι ≫ α' = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map T.f ≫ JB.ι)
    (hβ' : JB.ι ≫ β' = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map T.g ≫ JC.ι)
    (hexact : ∀ n : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).ShortExact)
    (hexact' : ∀ n : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α' β' hαβ').map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).ShortExact)
    (φA : IA.cocomplex ⟶ JA.cocomplex) (φC : IC.cocomplex ⟶ JC.cocomplex)
    (hφA : IA.ι ≫ φA = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map F.τ₁ ≫ JA.ι)
    (hφC : IC.ι ≫ φC = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map F.τ₃ ≫ JC.ι)
    (t : ∀ n, IB.cocomplex.X n ⟶ JB.cocomplex.X n)
    (htα : ∀ n, α.f n ≫ t n = φA.f n ≫ α'.f n)
    (htβ : ∀ n, t n ≫ β'.f n = β.f n ≫ φC.f n) :
    ∃ (E : ∀ n, IC.cocomplex.X n ⟶ JA.cocomplex.X (n + 1))
      (e : S.X₃ ⟶ JA.cocomplex.X 0),
      (∀ n, β.f n ≫ E n ≫ α'.f (n + 1) =
        t n ≫ JB.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) - IB.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) ≫ t (n + 1)) ∧
      S.g ≫ e ≫ α'.f 0 =
        IB.ι.f 0 ≫ t 0 - ((CochainComplex.single₀ C).map F.τ₂ ≫ JB.ι).f 0 ∧
      IC.ι.f 0 ≫ E 0 = e ≫ JA.cocomplex.d 0 1 ∧
      ∀ n, IC.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) ≫ E (n + 1) =
        -(E n ≫ JA.cocomplex.d (n + 1) (n + 2))
